messages:
Samir Patel: Quick heads-up — profiled a 72h window and saw persistent tail latency spikes on long-seq tenants when short-seq traffic peaks. KV hit ratios are stable but long lanes are getting queued behind small fast batches. Suspect continuous-batcher is biasing toward fill-rate over fairness.
Jules Nguyen: Can you share the top traces? Are we seeing kernel selection churn (FP16->INT8) or just scheduling delays?
Samir Patel: Traces attached (excerpt):
```
2026-02-25T14:02:10Z tenant=t4 seq=2048 kernel=fast_attn_v2 batch_size=1 queued=320ms
2026-02-25T14:02:10Z tenant=t9 seq=32 kernel=fast_attn_v2 batch_size=64 queued=12ms
```
We see long seq requests getting single-item microbatches and waiting for slot refill; meanwhile short seq flows coalesce into big batches. Kernel selection stable; problem is batch formation + token-budget refill policy.
Priya Rao: Interesting. So short flows get throughput wins because they piggyback on a large batch. Maybe we need a token-target allocator per-lane that reserves headroom for long sequences? Also consider preemptive KV warmup for long seqs (warm KV cache entries to avoid first-token stutter).
Miguel Ortiz: +1 for per-lane token budgets. We experimented with 'deferred-credit' in Q3 — reserve X tokens per long-lane every epoch and only allow surplus to be used by shorts. Might be worth re-trying with adaptive X based on seq-length histogram.
Samir Patel: Proposed experiment: introduce two changes behind flags:
1) lane_token_target: long=2048tokens_per_epoch, short=256tokens_per_epoch (adaptive via EWMA)
2) preemptive_kv_warmup: kick off KV fetch for head positions when a long request enters queue for >Yms
Config snippet:
```
{"lane_policy": "two_lane",
 "token_targets": {"long": 2048, "short": 256},
 "kv_warmup_threshold_ms": 80}
```
Jules Nguyen: Need to be careful with memory pressure if we over-warm KV for many tenants. Maybe limit warmup concurrency per-GPU.
Priya Rao: Agreed — add a token_cost cap so warmup only happens if expected cost < threshold. Also add metric: kv_warmup_hit_ratio and long_tail_p99_latency_by_tenant.
kv-monitor-bot: alert: long_seq_p99 > 750ms for tenant t4 (window 30m) — investigating.
Miguel Ortiz: We should run a canary on dedicated pool A with synthetic mix: 10% long(>1k), 90% short(<=64) and compare p99/p50 and fairness score (p99_long/p99_short). I'll prepare job.
Samir Patel: Thanks. Also want minimal changes to kernel selection logic — keep that stable. Aim to avoid preemption costs; prioritize queue-level crediting and KV warmup first. If canary looks good, we'll rollout canary -> staged -> global.
Jules Nguyen: I'll add dashboards and a slice in console: per-tenant fairness index + kv_warmup metrics. Ping me when canary job link is ready @Jules.
Priya Rao: I'll own the threshold tuning. Miguel can you paste the synthetic workload config when ready?
Miguel Ortiz: Will do, ETA 2h. Posting synthetic config and initial results in this thread when available :rocket:
Samir Patel: Great — thanks all. If we see regression, rollback flag is `lane_token_target=off` and `kv_warmup=false`. Keep thread for results.
